posts.text: 🕊️ Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez expressed his government’s solidarity on Friday with the authorities, the Egyptian people, and the families of the victims of the accident that occurred north of Cairo, and wished those injured a speedy recovery. 💥 The incident occurred last Wednesday on the Warraq highway when a cargo truck carrying gas cylinders and petroleum products suffered a mechanical failure in the steering system, crashed into a concrete barrier, and caught fire. 🚒 The official toll confirmed thirty-one dead, twenty-one injured, and dozens of cars destroyed by the fire in the Giza Governorate.

📝 Long vacant no more 📝 on warehouses and arsenals on the territory of so-called Ukraine The first year of the SMO saw active strikes by the Russian Armed Forces on warehouses and arsenals with weapons and ammunition . Some succeeded, while others, after one or two impacts, the facility received the status of "destroyed," and everyone conveniently forgot about it. What this led to more than once is, in principle, obvious. If a territory does not appear on strike lists, but it is fortified, protected, and has access to logistics routes, why not use it? This is exactly what happened with the 10th AFU arsenal in Voznesensk , which took a hit from a Geran. 🔻 Why is it important? ▪️ This facility belongs to the category of strategic warehouses for rocket and artillery weapons under the control of AFU logistics command. Historically, since 1946, ammunition has been stored there (primarily cartridges for small arms, machine guns, grenades for AGS-17). ▪️ They also kept barrel artillery there – anti-tank guns MT-12, D-20 howitzers, Msta-B and Hyacinth-B, as well as multiple rocket launchers like Grads and Hurricanes. 🖍️ They struck it (and that's not even certain) only twice during the SMO. In August 2022, and then in autumn 2023. That's it. The territory essentially remained untouched for many years. Given that Voznesensk is an important logistics hub, the use of the 10th arsenal is quite expected. Of course, it's hard to believe that Soviet weapons system ammunition is stored there now, since the AFU exhausted their reserves a couple of years ago. But! From the Voznesensk area, drones are regularly launched at Crimea and Krasnodar Region, and Bayraktars and sometimes tactical aviation fly from the airfield. ❗️ And there are many such warehouses on the territory of so-called Ukraine (thanks to Soviet legacy) that continue to be used for their intended purpose, which raises the question of the need for systematic fire on such targets. If they are stationary, that doesn't mean they won't be used. If nothing is hitting them, then why not? #Voznesensk #Russia #Ukraine ✉ MAX 💸 Support us Original msg

The World Health Organization warns of a rapid rise in meningitis cases among children in Gaza since mid-October, as displaced families live in tents amid destroyed water and sewage networks and mounting waste. The WHO says essential laboratory supplies are barred from entering Gaza and critical medical supplies are running short, leaving doctors unable to tell viral meningitis from bacterial meningitis. Infants make up most of the cases. More than 533 cases and four deaths have been reported since mid-October, and Gaza's Health Ministry has declared an "epidemic alert."

Visioner BIG | 🇩🇪 🇺🇦 ‼️ ‼️ Germany has approved its 2027 federal budget, allocating approximately €12 billion to support Ukraine while raising defense spending to nearly €140 billion. The approved budget includes around €12 billion in assistance for Ukraine, reflecting Berlin’s continued commitment to supporting Kyiv. Germany’s overall defense expenditure is set to reach almost €140 billion, while total new borrowing is expected to amount to approximately €210 billion. The figures highlight the scale of Germany’s planned military spending and financial commitments. The substantial allocation for Ukraine signals Berlin’s intention to maintain long-term support for Kyiv as Russia’s war continues. At the same time, Germany’s increased defense spending reflects a broader European effort to strengthen military capabilities and prepare for potential security threats. Together, these commitments could play an important role in sustaining Ukraine’s defense and reinforcing NATO’s European forces. See the latest updates with us: @visionergeo tweet

Visioner BIG | 🇷🇺 🇺🇦 ‼️ ‼️ At least 87 officers from Russia’s highly secretive Special Operations Forces (SSO) have died since the beginning of the full-scale war against Ukraine, according to an investigation by the independent Russian outlet Important Stories, based on leaked Rosstat records. The investigation identified 54 officers killed in Ukraine and another three who died from their wounds in Russian hospitals. Five reportedly died in Syria, while another five were killed inside Russia in operations attributed to Ukrainian intelligence services. The remaining deaths occurred under non-combat or unclear circumstances. Russia’s SSO is an elite military formation whose personnel are selected from special forces units, including those associated with the GRU. Its estimated strength ranges from 2,500 to 7,000 personnel. The force participated in the 2014 annexation of Crimea, operations involving former Ukrainian President Viktor Yanukovych, and Russia’s military campaign in Syria. According to The Wall Street Journal, personnel from the unit later joined a military intelligence structure linked to sabotage operations in NATO countries. The reported deaths are significant because Russia’s SSO relies on highly trained personnel who are difficult and expensive to replace. Losses among experienced officers can weaken operational planning, reconnaissance, and specialized missions. The findings also offer a rare glimpse into casualties within one of Russia’s most secretive military formations. See the latest updates with us: @visionergeo tweet

Visioner BIG | 🇮🇷 🇺🇦 🇮🇹 ‼️ ‼️ Iran has accused Ukraine of carrying out a deadly attack in Kuwait and attempting to blame Tehran, despite Italy and Kuwait holding Iran responsible for the incident. No evidence has been presented to support the accusation against Ukraine. According to the Iranian account, Ukraine allegedly organized the strike while presenting it as an Iranian attack. Tehran claims Kyiv, which has reportedly deployed specialists to the Middle East to help counter Iranian drones, wanted to draw European countries into the conflict with Iran while demonstrating its strategic value to US President Donald Trump. The attack reportedly killed two Italian military specialists associated with Rheinmetall. Italian and Kuwaiti authorities, however, attribute responsibility for the incident to Iran. The accusation comes amid tensions involving Iran, Ukraine, and Western countries. Tehran’s allegations attempt to shift responsibility for the deadly incident onto Kyiv, but without supporting evidence, there is no basis for treating Ukrainian involvement as established. The competing accounts also show how accusations surrounding military attacks can become part of a wider diplomatic confrontation. See the latest updates with us: @visionergeo tweet

Visioner BREAKING | 🇮🇷 🇺🇸 ‼️ ‼️ Iran’s IRGC claims its air defenses fired warning shots at a US Air Force F-16C Fighting Falcon near Hengam Island in the Strait of Hormuz, forcing the American fighter jet to perform an evasive maneuver and withdraw. According to the IRGC Aerospace Force, the US aircraft was flying southeast of Hengam Island when Iranian air defenses engaged it with warning fire. Tehran warned that further alleged violations of Iranian airspace would face a decisive response, referring to the reported downing of a US F-15E Strike Eagle earlier this year. Earlier reports also described fighter jet activity over southeastern Qeshm Island and a surface-to-air missile launch from Toula, on the island’s eastern side. The Iranian account of the F-16 incident has not been independently verified, and no US confirmation has been provided. The reported encounter highlights the danger of direct military confrontation between US and Iranian forces around the Strait of Hormuz. The presence of fighter aircraft and active air defense systems in such a sensitive area increases the risk of miscalculation, particularly when both sides are operating in close proximity. Even a warning engagement could escalate rapidly into a wider confrontation. See the latest updates with us: @visionergeo tweet

The US military struck and disabled a commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman, the US Central Command (CENTCOM) said. “CENTCOM disabled a commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman, Nov. 26, after the crew attempted to run the US naval blockade, despite multiple warnings, following departure from Bandar Abbas,” it said. “A US military aircraft launched precision munitions that struck the stern of Palau-flagged M/V Pacific Archer. The ship’s propulsion was ultimately disabled and the civilian crew was unharmed.”
